tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

- This tool will overwrite the existing file if there is one at the provided path.
- If this is an existing file, you MUST use the Read tool first to read the file's contents. This tool will fail if you did not read the file first.

- NEVER create documentation files (*.md) or README files unless explicitly requested by the User.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid writing emojis to files unless asked.

1	# Implementation Plan: P-RF05 — Personal summary export
2	
3	**Branch**: `010-personal-summary-export` (spec directory only — no git branch exists; none of this repo's
4	extension hooks are configured, per spec.md's own header)
5	
6	**Date**: 2026-10-24 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
7	
8	**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/010-personal-summary-export/spec.md`, `docs/input/requirements.md`
9	§1 (RF05), §6.5 (`export-summary-create`/`export-status-get`/`export-download-get`), §8 (data model
10	reference), §9 (stack), §13; `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`'s `/export/*` schemas;
11	`docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md`; `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`;
12	`docs/input/backend/README.md`'s function-name mapping; `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §2.5; and
13	`.specify/memory/constitution.md`. Depends on RF07 (`specs/005-multi-source-timeline/`), already implemented —
14	this is the unit that makes "Meus Registros"' currently-inert download icon
15	(`records_page.dart`'s `_Header`, comment "no export behavior in this unit") actually work.
16	
17	## Summary
18	
19	"Meus Registros"' download icon gains a bottom sheet (`ExportSheet`) that requests an async export job for
20	whatever period the screen's own active date filter represents (`POST /export/summary`), polls its status
21	(`GET /export/{jobId}/status`) every 2 seconds, and — once the job reaches a terminal state — offers a PDF
22	narrative download and/or a raw-data download (`GET /export/{jobId}/download`), each saved/shared via the OS
23	share sheet. A new feature folder, `lib/features/export/`, is added with its own three-layer structure:
24	`ExportJob`/`ExportFormat`/`ExportSheetState` (domain, plus a pure `sheetState` derivation of
25	`export-screen-states.md`'s table), `ExportRepository`/`ExportFileRepository` (domain interfaces),
26	`ExportRemoteDataSource`/`ExportRepositoryImpl`/`ExportFileRepositoryImpl` (data), and one bloc, `ExportBloc`
27	(one new instance per sheet open, research.md R6). `core/network/ApiClient` gains one new, export-agnostic
28	method, `downloadFile()` — a two-step fetch (our backend's 302, then a header-less GET of the signed Storage
29	URL) that never forwards this app's own credentials to the Storage host (research.md R1). A new dependency,
30	`share_plus`, provides the "save or share" affordance no existing package in this app covers. The spec's own
31	resolved Clarification — a sixth, generic failure state distinct from the prototype's one narrative-only
32	"Erro" — is implemented as a sixth `ExportSheetState`/`ExportState` value, `erroCompleto`/`ExportFailed`
33	(research.md R4). `records_page.dart`'s `_Header`/`_RecordsPageState` are extended in place to wire the icon
34	to the sheet, deriving the period from `RecordsBloc`'s existing `DateRangeOption` via RF06's own
35	`DateRangeBounds` extension (research.md R8) — no new `RecordsBloc` event/state, no new `go_router` route.
36	
37	## Technical Context
38	
39	**Language/Version**: Dart 3.13.4 / Flutter 3.47.5 (stable), pinned via `.fvmrc` — unchanged from
40	F000/RF01/RF03/RF06/RF07.
41	
42	**Primary Dependencies**: One addition — `share_plus: ^13.3.1` (research.md R2), the OS share sheet for the
43	two downloadable files this unit produces. Everything else reuses the full existing stack —
44	`flutter_bloc`, `fpdart`, `get_it`, `equatable`, `dio` (via `ApiClient`, extended with `downloadFile()`),
45	`path_provider` (already present for the audio pipeline, reused here for a temp file), `go_router` (no new
46	route); dev-only `mocktail`, `bloc_test`.
47	
48	**Storage**: None new. `export_jobs`/their downloaded files are explicitly ephemeral (Key Entities: "never
49	shown anywhere outside the export sheet") — unlike `EntriesLocalCache`/`ChatLocalCache`, this unit adds no
50	on-device persistence; a downloaded file lives only in the OS temp directory for the lifetime of the share
51	sheet.
52	
53	**Testing**: `flutter_test` + `bloc_test` + `mocktail`, unchanged tooling. Coverage via `fvm flutter test
54	--coverage`, same `lib/**/domain/**` lcov filter (RNF07), now additionally exercising `export_job.dart`'s pure
55	`sheetState` mapping (R4), `ExportRepositoryImpl`'s silent-refresh-and-retry branches (reused verbatim from
56	`EntriesRepositoryImpl`'s shape), and `ApiClient.downloadFile()`'s two-leg redirect/fetch logic (a `core/`
57	addition — `test/core/network/`, mirroring where `sse_frame`/`error_mapper` tests already live).
58	
59	**Target Platform**: iOS, portrait only — unchanged. No native project file touched beyond whatever
60	`share_plus`'s own iOS integration requires at the `Info.plist`/Podfile level (its own install instructions;
61	no custom native code written by this unit).
62	
63	**Project Type**: Same single Flutter mobile app. One new feature folder, `lib/features/export/`
64	(domain/data/presentation, Principle V), one cross-cutting `core/network/` addition
65	(`ApiClient.downloadFile()`), and in-place extensions to `lib/features/records/presentation/pages/
66	records_page.dart` (`_Header`/`_RecordsPageState`, research.md R8) and `lib/core/di/service_locator.dart`. No
67	backend/server code, no change to `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`.
68	
69	**Performance Goals**: RNF01 unchanged. The sheet's "Pendente" state appears synchronously the instant the
70	download icon is tapped (before the `POST` even resolves), satisfying "a local action is reflected in the UI
71	in under 100 ms"; the `POST`/polling/download calls themselves are each already covered by the loading-
72	indicator convention their own sheet states already are (spinner/progress bar), satisfying "any network call
73	taking longer than 300 ms MUST show a loading indicator" by construction — there is no network call in this
74	unit's flow that is ever silent.
75	
76	**Constraints**:
77	- No manual-tag/category filtering or any other extension feature (FR-013) — the export sheet has no period
78	  picker, no persona/categorization control of its own.
79	- No functionality belonging to a unit later than RF05 in the build order (FR-013) — RF09's dashboard
80	  narrative (`GET /dashboard/narrative`) is a distinct endpoint, never touched here.
81	- No backend/contract/config change (FR-013) — `downloadFile()`'s two-leg shape and every parsed field name
82	  (research.md R1/contracts/export-repository.md) are this app's own typed wrapper around what
83	  `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml` already describes.
84	- Clean Architecture, 3 layers per feature (Principle V) — `export/domain/` imports only
85	  `equatable`/`fpdart`; no `package:flutter`, no `export/data/` class. `ExportBloc` depends only on
86	  `ExportRepository`/`ExportFileRepository` — never `SessionRepository` directly (research.md R7), never
87	  `RecordsBloc` (no cross-bloc import).
88	- FR-011's concurrency guard is satisfied by construction, not by a shared/persisted job id: a sheet-scoped,
89	  `registerFactory`-registered `ExportBloc` (research.md R6) plus a simple tap-guard in
90	  `_RecordsPageState` (research.md R8/contracts/records-header-export-extension.md) — no second
91	  `POST /export/summary` can fire for the same tap, and no in-flight job is polled once its sheet is gone.
92	- Zero visual values hardcoded outside `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` (Principle IV/RNF08) — every new widget
93	  reuses existing tokens only (data-model.md's widget list) — zero new color/spacing/radius tokens needed,
94	  since `colorAccent`/`colorSuccess`/`colorError` already exist from F000/RF06/RF07.
95	
96	**Scale/Scope**: 1 new feature folder (`export/`) with 1 domain entity + 1 pure derivation extension, 2
97	repository interfaces, 2 data classes + 2 repository impls, 1 bloc (+events/states), 7 new presentation
98	widgets; 1 extended `core/network/` method (`ApiClient.downloadFile()`); 1 existing `records/` file extended
99	in place (`records_page.dart`); 1 new dependency (`share_plus`); 5 new DI registrations.
100	
101	## Constitution Check
102	
103	*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-checked after Phase 1 design — see bottom of this section.*
104	
105	| Principle / Standard | Status | Notes |
106	|---|---|---|
107	| I. Product Source of Truth | PASS | `docs/input/` read-only. Every spot this plan resolves by reasonable technical judgment rather than reopening spec.md's own already-resolved Clarification (the FR-007 sixth state) — the download-transport mechanism (research.md R1), the file-save/share package (R2), the poll interval (R3), the sheet-state derivation and its sixth value (R4), routing non-empty-period `POST` failures to FR-007 (R5), the sheet-scoped-bloc concurrency shape (R6), the reauth wiring (R7), and period-bounds plumbing (R8) — is each built directly on spec.md's own FRs/Assumptions/Key Entities wording, never reopening the resolved Clarification. |
108	| II. Fixed Technology Stack | PASS | No change to `flutter_bloc`/`fpdart`/`get_it`/Clean Architecture. One new dependency, `share_plus` — squarely inside Principle II's own "choices not fixed here... local cache... secure storage" open-decision category (no fixed file-share package is named anywhere in `docs/input/`), the same category `image_picker`/`record`/`whisper_ggml` were already added under. |
109	| III. Backend Boundary | PASS | Only already-contracted functions called (`export-summary-create`, `export-status-get`, `export-download-get` — `docs/input/backend/README.md`'s own path→function table); no AI provider called directly (Claude Haiku 4.5's summary generation stays entirely server-side). `downloadFile()`'s header-less second leg (research.md R1) exists specifically *to protect* this app's own `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`/bearer token from being forwarded to a host outside the documented contract — reinforcing, not weakening, Principle III's credential-leakage concern. |
110	| IV. Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity | PASS | Every new widget reuses existing `DesignTokens` entries only (data-model.md's widget list, sourced from `prototype-extract.md` §2.5's own five-state description plus the resolved Clarification's sixth) — zero new tokens. UI text ("Preparando exportação...", "Gerando resumo com IA...", "Resumo pronto", "Baixar PDF", "Baixar dados brutos", "Nenhum registro nesse período.", "Fechar") is exactly as the prototype extract and spec.md's own FR wording state it, in Portuguese; the one genuinely new copy this unit must author (FR-007's generic failure text, since the prototype names no sixth state) is written in Portuguese consistent with the other four states' register and tone. |
111	| V. Clean Architecture Folder Convention | PASS | `export/domain/` imports only `equatable`/`fpdart`/`core/network/failure.dart` — confirmed against `domain_purity_test.dart` (unmodified). `ExportBloc`'s dependency surface is exactly `ExportRepository`/`ExportFileRepository` — no `SessionBloc`, no `RecordsBloc` import. |
112	| RNF01 (latency) | PASS | See Technical Context's own Performance Goals entry above — every network call in this unit's flow already shows a loading indicator (one of the sheet's own five-or-six states) by construction; "Pendente" itself is the sub-100ms local reflection. |
113	| RNF02/03/04 (PII, retention, RLS) | N/A to RF05 | Backend-side; this unit sends no new PII-bearing content of its own (the export request carries only a date range, never entry content) and introduces no new on-device retention (Technical Context's own Storage entry: none). |
114	| RNF05 (hard delete) | N/A to RF05 | Belongs to Settings/RNF05's own unit. |
115	| RNF06 (layer violations) | PASS | No `export/domain/` file imports Flutter or an `export/data/` class; `ExportBloc` imports neither `SessionBloc` nor `RecordsBloc` — `no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart`/`domain_purity_test.dart` both continue to pass unmodified against the new folder. |
116	| RNF07 (domain coverage ≥80%) | PASS (gate carried into tasks) | `export_job.dart`'s `sheetState` extension is a pure, total function over a 5×5 enum pair, as directly testable as `date_range_filter.dart` (RF06)/`sync_badge_state.dart` (RF07); `ExportRepositoryImpl`'s retry branches are testable against the same `mocktail` fakes `EntriesRepositoryImpl`'s own tests already use the pattern for. |
117	| RNF08 (visual fidelity) | PASS | The six sheet states match `prototype-extract.md` §2.5 (five named states) plus the resolved Clarification's sixth exactly — no approximated layout or invented component beyond what spec.md/the prototype already name. |
118	| RNF09 (Either + 15/15 error scenarios) | PASS (gate carried into tasks) | RF05 adds one new write endpoint to the project-wide tally, `export-summary-create` (`POST`) — its 3 required failure scenarios (timeout, malformed response, no-connection) are exercised exactly as rigorously as every prior write endpoint's, per `contracts/export-repository.md`'s own scenario table (items 3/5). `export-status-get`/`export-download-get` are `GET`s, outside RNF09's "5 write endpoints" tally, but are still fully `Either`-typed and covered by `contracts/export-repository.md`/`contracts/http-client-download-extension.md`'s own scenario tables regardless. |
119	
120	*Post-Phase-1 re-check: see "Post-Design Constitution Check" at the end of this document.*
121

180	
181	**Structure Decision**: One new feature folder, `export/`, following the exact three-layer convention every
182	prior unit already established — no deviation. The one `core/network/` addition (`ApiClient.downloadFile()`)
183	lives there rather than inside `export/` because it is not export-specific in shape (any future signed-URL-
184	download unit reuses it as-is, same reasoning RF04's `sseStream()` was placed in `core/network/` rather than
185	inside `chat/`). `records/` is extended rather than having the export sheet folded into it because the sheet
186	is its own independently-testable concern (its own bloc, its own repository boundary) that only happens to be
187	*opened from* "Meus Registros" — exactly the same "extend the opening screen in place, give the new concern
188	its own feature folder" shape RF06's `FilterSheet` already established within `records/` itself (the one
189	difference being `FilterSheet` has no bloc of its own, needing no separate feature folder, while the export
190	sheet's async job/polling/download concern is large enough to warrant one, mirroring `chat/`'s own
191	`AppDrawer`-extension-plus-new-feature-folder precedent).
192	
193	## Complexity Tracking
194	
195	| Addition | Why Needed | Simpler Alternative Rejected Because |
196	|---|---|---|
197	| A second `ApiClient` transport primitive, `downloadFile()` (research.md R1) | `export-download-get` is this app's first endpoint whose success response is a 302-to-a-signed-URL, not JSON — `call()`'s existing `Dio.request<Map<String, dynamic>>()` cannot parse a redirect target's binary bytes, and naively letting `dio` auto-follow the redirect would forward this app's own auth headers to a third-party Storage host | Letting `dio` auto-follow redirects and reusing `call()` as-is — rejected: leaks `apikey`/bearer-token headers to a host they were never scoped for (research.md R1) |
198	| A new dependency, `share_plus` | This app has no existing mechanism for "hand the user a file to save or share" — `path_provider` alone only produces a path, never a UI affordance to do anything with it | Writing to a permanent path with no share prompt — rejected, a dead end with no in-app file viewer in scope (research.md R2) |
199	| A sixth `ExportSheetState`/`ExportState` value (`erroCompleto`/`ExportFailed`), beyond the prototype's five named states | The resolved Clarification explicitly requires a failure state "visually and functionally distinct" from the prototype's one narrative-only "Erro" — collapsing both into one state with a flag would directly contradict that resolution | One shared `erro` state with a boolean "is this the narrative-only case" flag — rejected per the Clarification's own explicit wording (research.md R4) |
200	
201	*No entry needed beyond these three — each is either this unit's first genuinely new mechanism (the
202	redirect-download transport, the file-share dependency) or a direct, required encoding of spec.md's own
203	already-resolved Clarification (the sixth state).*
204	
205	## Post-Design Constitution Check
206	
207	Re-evaluated after Phase 1 (data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md):
208	
209	- `export/domain/entities/export_job.dart` and both `export/domain/repositories/*.dart` were re-checked
210	  against their actual planned imports: `equatable`, `fpdart` (for `Either`/`Unit` signatures), and
211	  `core/network/failure.dart` only. No `package:flutter`, no `export/data/` class — RNF06/Principle V
212	  confirmed before any code exists.
213	- `ExportBloc`'s dependency surface was re-checked: exactly `ExportRepository` + `ExportFileRepository` — no
214	  `SessionRepository`, no `RecordsBloc` import. Neither `ExportBloc` nor `RecordsBloc` appears in the other's
215	  planned import list (`no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart` covers this mechanically across `features/` folders).
216	- Re-checked `ApiClient.downloadFile()`'s exception handling against `call()`'s existing `_mapException` —
217	  reused verbatim for leg 1; leg 2's storage-host failures fall through the same function's existing no-JSON-
218	  body branch, so no second, divergent failure-mapping implementation was introduced.
219	- Re-checked that the second `_dio.request` in `downloadFile()` (the storage leg) sends no
220	  `apikey`/`Authorization` header at all — confirmed in `contracts/http-client-download-extension.md`'s own
221	  code listing (Principle III's credential-exposure concern, research.md R1).
222	- Re-checked that `ExportJob.sheetState`, the one domain helper RNF07 specifically needs to be independently
223	  testable, has zero constructor dependencies and zero I/O — confirmed pure in data-model.md's own listing.
224	- Re-checked the `records_page.dart` extension (research.md R8) against Principle V: no new `RecordsEvent`/

# Implementation Plan: P-RF05 — Personal summary export

**Branch**: `010-personal-summary-export` (spec directory only — no git branch exists; none of this repo's
extension hooks are configured, per spec.md's own header)

**Date**: 2026-10-24 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/010-personal-summary-export/spec.md`, `docs/input/requirements.md`
§1 (RF05), §6.5 (`export-summary-create`/`export-status-get`/`export-download-get`), §8 (data model
reference), §9 (stack), §13; `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`'s `/export/*` schemas;
`docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md`; `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`;
`docs/input/backend/README.md`'s function-name mapping; `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §2.5; and
`.specify/memory/constitution.md`. Depends on RF07 (`specs/005-multi-source-timeline/`), already implemented —
this is the unit that makes "Meus Registros"' currently-inert download icon
(`records_page.dart`'s `_Header`, comment "no export behavior in this unit") actually work.

## Summary

"Meus Registros"' download icon gains a bottom sheet (`ExportSheet`) that requests an async export job for
whatever period the screen's own active date filter represents (`POST /export/summary`), polls its status
(`GET /export/{jobId}/status`) every 2 seconds, and — once the job reaches a terminal state — offers a PDF
narrative download and/or a raw-data download (`GET /export/{jobId}/download`), each saved/shared via the OS
share sheet. A new feature folder, `lib/features/export/`, is added with its own three-layer structure:
`ExportJob`/`ExportFormat`/`ExportSheetState` (domain, plus a pure `sheetState` derivation of
`export-screen-states.md`'s table), `ExportRepository`/`ExportFileRepository` (domain interfaces),
`ExportRemoteDataSource`/`ExportRepositoryImpl`/`ExportFileRepositoryImpl` (data), and one bloc, `ExportBloc`
(one new instance per sheet open, research.md R6). `core/network/ApiClient` gains one new, export-agnostic
method, `downloadFile()` — a two-step fetch (our backend's 302, then a header-less GET of the signed Storage
URL) that never forwards this app's own credentials to the Storage host (research.md R1). A new dependency,
`share_plus`, provides the "save or share" affordance no existing package in this app covers. The spec's own
resolved Clarification — a sixth, generic failure state distinct from the prototype's one narrative-only
"Erro" — is implemented as a sixth `ExportSheetState`/`ExportState` value, `erroCompleto`/`ExportFailed`
(research.md R4). `records_page.dart`'s `_Header`/`_RecordsPageState` are extended in place to wire the icon
to the sheet, deriving the period from `RecordsBloc`'s existing `DateRangeOption` via RF06's own
`DateRangeBounds` extension (research.md R8) — no new `RecordsBloc` event/state, no new `go_router` route.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Dart 3.13.4 / Flutter 3.47.5 (stable), pinned via `.fvmrc` — unchanged from
F000/RF01/RF03/RF06/RF07.

**Primary Dependencies**: One addition — `share_plus: ^13.3.1` (research.md R2), the OS share sheet for the
two downloadable files this unit produces. Everything else reuses the full existing stack —
`flutter_bloc`, `fpdart`, `get_it`, `equatable`, `dio` (via `ApiClient`, extended with `downloadFile()`),
`path_provider` (already present for the audio pipeline, reused here for a temp file), `go_router` (no new
route); dev-only `mocktail`, `bloc_test`.

**Storage**: None new. `export_jobs`/their downloaded files are explicitly ephemeral (Key Entities: "never
shown anywhere outside the export sheet") — unlike `EntriesLocalCache`/`ChatLocalCache`, this unit adds no
on-device persistence; a downloaded file lives only in the OS temp directory for the lifetime of the share
sheet.

**Testing**: `flutter_test` + `bloc_test` + `mocktail`, unchanged tooling. Coverage via `fvm flutter test
--coverage`, same `lib/**/domain/**` lcov filter (RNF07), now additionally exercising `export_job.dart`'s pure
`sheetState` mapping (R4), `ExportRepositoryImpl`'s silent-refresh-and-retry branches (reused verbatim from
`EntriesRepositoryImpl`'s shape), and `ApiClient.downloadFile()`'s two-leg redirect/fetch logic (a `core/`
addition — `test/core/network/`, mirroring where `sse_frame`/`error_mapper` tests already live).

**Target Platform**: iOS, portrait only — unchanged. No native project file touched beyond whatever
`share_plus`'s own iOS integration requires at the `Info.plist`/Podfile level (its own install instructions;
no custom native code written by this unit).

**Project Type**: Same single Flutter mobile app. One new feature folder, `lib/features/export/`
(domain/data/presentation, Principle V), one cross-cutting `core/network/` addition
(`ApiClient.downloadFile()`), and in-place extensions to `lib/features/records/presentation/pages/
records_page.dart` (`_Header`/`_RecordsPageState`, research.md R8) and `lib/core/di/service_locator.dart`. No
backend/server code, no change to `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`.

**Performance Goals**: RNF01 unchanged. The sheet's "Pendente" state appears synchronously the instant the
download icon is tapped (before the `POST` even resolves), satisfying "a local action is reflected in the UI
in under 100 ms"; the `POST`/polling/download calls themselves are each already covered by the loading-
indicator convention their own sheet states already are (spinner/progress bar), satisfying "any network call
taking longer than 300 ms MUST show a loading indicator" by construction — there is no network call in this
unit's flow that is ever silent.

**Constraints**:
- No manual-tag/category filtering or any other extension feature (FR-013) — the export sheet has no period
  picker, no persona/categorization control of its own.
- No functionality belonging to a unit later than RF05 in the build order (FR-013) — RF09's dashboard
  narrative (`GET /dashboard/narrative`) is a distinct endpoint, never touched here.
- No backend/contract/config change (FR-013) — `downloadFile()`'s two-leg shape and every parsed field name
  (research.md R1/contracts/export-repository.md) are this app's own typed wrapper around what
  `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml` already describes.
- Clean Architecture, 3 layers per feature (Principle V) — `export/domain/` imports only
  `equatable`/`fpdart`; no `package:flutter`, no `export/data/` class. `ExportBloc` depends only on
  `ExportRepository`/`ExportFileRepository` — never `SessionRepository` directly (research.md R7), never
  `RecordsBloc` (no cross-bloc import).
- FR-011's concurrency guard is satisfied by construction, not by a shared/persisted job id: a sheet-scoped,
  `registerFactory`-registered `ExportBloc` (research.md R6) plus a simple tap-guard in
  `_RecordsPageState` (research.md R8/contracts/records-header-export-extension.md) — no second
  `POST /export/summary` can fire for the same tap, and no in-flight job is polled once its sheet is gone.
- Zero visual values hardcoded outside `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` (Principle IV/RNF08) — every new widget
  reuses existing tokens only (data-model.md's widget list) — zero new color/spacing/radius tokens needed,
  since `colorAccent`/`colorSuccess`/`colorError` already exist from F000/RF06/RF07.

**Scale/Scope**: 1 new feature folder (`export/`) with 1 domain entity + 1 pure derivation extension, 2
repository interfaces, 2 data classes + 2 repository impls, 1 bloc (+events/states), 7 new presentation
widgets; 1 extended `core/network/` method (`ApiClient.downloadFile()`); 1 existing `records/` file extended
in place (`records_page.dart`); 1 new dependency (`share_plus`); 5 new DI registrations.

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-checked after Phase 1 design — see bottom of this section.*

| Principle / Standard | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| I. Product Source of Truth | PASS | `docs/input/` read-only. Every spot this plan resolves by reasonable technical judgment rather than reopening spec.md's own already-resolved Clarification (the FR-007 sixth state) — the download-transport mechanism (research.md R1), the file-save/share package (R2), the poll interval (R3), the sheet-state derivation and its sixth value (R4), routing non-empty-period `POST` failures to FR-007 (R5), the sheet-scoped-bloc concurrency shape (R6), the reauth wiring (R7), and period-bounds plumbing (R8) — is each built directly on spec.md's own FRs/Assumptions/Key Entities wording, never reopening the resolved Clarification. |
| II. Fixed Technology Stack | PASS | No change to `flutter_bloc`/`fpdart`/`get_it`/Clean Architecture. One new dependency, `share_plus` — squarely inside Principle II's own "choices not fixed here... local cache... secure storage" open-decision category (no fixed file-share package is named anywhere in `docs/input/`), the same category `image_picker`/`record`/`whisper_ggml` were already added under. |

Backend Boundary | PASS | Only already-contracted functions called (`export-summary-create`, `export-status-get`, `export-download-get` — `docs/input/backend/README.md`'s own path→function table); no AI provider called directly (Claude Haiku 4.5's summary generation stays entirely server-side). `downloadFile()`'s header-less second leg (research.md R1) exists specifically *to protect* this app's own `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`/bearer token from being forwarded to a host outside the documented contract — reinforcing, not weakening, Principle III's credential-leakage concern. |

Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity | PASS | Every new widget reuses existing `DesignTokens` entries only (data-model.md's widget list, sourced from `prototype-extract.md` §2.5's own five-state description plus the resolved Clarification's sixth) — zero new tokens. UI text ("Preparando exportação...", "Gerando resumo com IA...", "Resumo pronto", "Baixar PDF", "Baixar dados brutos", "Nenhum registro nesse período.", "Fechar") is exactly as the prototype extract and spec.md's own FR wording state it, in Portuguese; the one genuinely new copy this unit must author (FR-007's generic failure text, since the prototype names no sixth state) is written in Portuguese consistent with the other four states' register and tone. |

# Feature Specification: P-RF05 — Personal summary export

**Feature Branch**: `010-personal-summary-export` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)

**Created**: 2026-10-24

**Status**: Draft

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-10-24

- Q: What should the export sheet show when the job fails entirely (FR-007 — no data produced at all, not just the AI narrative), given the prototype only defines an "Erro" state for the narrative-only failure and has no visual for this harder case? → A: Generic failure message (reusing the error color/icon family, with copy distinct from FR-006's narrative-only explanation), no PDF/raw buttons, and only the existing "Fechar" link — no dedicated in-sheet retry control, and the same text is shown regardless of the backend's specific errorCode. Retrying means closing the sheet and tapping the download icon again (FR-011's existing path) (resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I).

**Input**: User description: "P-RF05 — Personal summary export: Let the user export a narrative summary of their entries as PDF, and always be able to download the raw data. Requirement and acceptance criteria: docs/input/requirements.md, section 1, RF05. Prototype states: the export sheet — 'Pendente', 'Processando', 'Concluído', 'Erro', 'Período vazio' (prototype extract, section 2.5); opened by the download icon of Meus Registros. Screen ↔ job status mapping: docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md. Backend: POST /export/summary, GET /export/:jobId/status, GET /export/:jobId/download. Depends on: RF07. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements, section 2), or change the backend."

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Getting a narrative PDF of your entries (Priority: P1)

From My Records, the user taps the download icon and asks to export a summary of their entries. They watch the export prepare and then generate an AI narrative, and end up with a PDF they can download that tells the story of that period, alongside their original entries.

**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF05 — a narrative export is the feature's main value. Without it reaching a downloadable PDF, the feature does not exist.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening the export sheet for a period that has at least one entry, letting the job run to completion, and confirming a PDF download succeeds and contains a narrative summary.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user is on My Records with at least one entry in the exported period, **When** they tap the download icon, **Then** the export sheet opens and shows "Pendente" (spinner, "Preparando exportação...").
2. **Given** the export sheet is showing "Pendente", **When** the backend starts generating the AI narrative, **Then** the sheet shows "Processando" ("Gerando resumo com IA...", progress bar) without the user doing anything further.
3. **Given** the job finishes with both the data and the narrative ready, **When** the sheet updates, **Then** it shows "Concluído" (green check, "Resumo pronto") with two enabled buttons — "Baixar PDF" (primary) and "Baixar dados brutos" (outline).
4. **Given** the sheet is showing "Concluído", **When** the user taps "Baixar PDF", **Then** the app downloads a PDF file containing the generated narrative summary for that period.

---

### User Story 2 - Your raw data is never held hostage by the AI narrative (Priority: P1)

Generating the narrative summary can fail — the AI call can time out or error out. When that happens, the user can still get their own data out: the export sheet explains that only the narrative failed and lets them download their raw entries anyway.

**Why this priority**: Called out explicitly as its own acceptance criterion ("a failure generating the narrative text still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure"). Without this, a flaky AI call would make a user's own data unreachable, which is a trust-breaking failure for a personal-data feature.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by forcing the narrative generation to fail (e.g., simulating an AI timeout) for a period that does have entries, and confirming the sheet still offers — and completes — a raw-data download.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the export job's data finished successfully but the narrative generation failed or was skipped, **When** the sheet updates, **Then** it shows "Erro" (red warning) with text explaining that the AI summary failed but the data remains available, and exactly one enabled button — "Baixar dados brutos" (no "Baixar PDF" option is shown).
2. **Given** the sheet is showing this "Erro" state, **When** the user taps "Baixar dados brutos", **Then** the download succeeds with the user's raw entry data, with no dependency on the narrative ever having completed.
3. **Given** the export job fails entirely (not only the narrative — no data was produced either), **When** the sheet updates, **Then** it shows a failure state with no download option at all, which is visibly a harder failure than the narrative-only case in Scenario 1 (nothing is available to download because nothing was produced).

---

### User Story 3 - Exporting a period with nothing in it is handled gracefully (Priority: P2)

The user requests an export for a period that turns out to have zero entries. Instead of an empty or broken PDF, or the app hanging, they get a clear message telling them there is nothing to export.

**Why this priority**: Called out explicitly as an acceptance criterion ("an export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state — not an empty PDF, not a crash"). It is a correctness guarantee as much as a UX one.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by requesting an export for a period known to contain zero entries and confirming the sheet shows the dedicated empty-period state immediately, with no job ever appearing to run and no file ever offered for download.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user selects a period with zero entries, **When** they request the export, **Then** the sheet shows "Período vazio" ("Nenhum registro nesse período." plus a suggestion to adjust the filter) directly — never "Pendente" or "Processando" first — and offers no download button.
2. **Given** the sheet is showing "Período vazio", **When** the user taps "Fechar", **Then** the sheet dismisses without having created any downloadable file and without affecting My Records' own list or filters.

---

### Edge Cases

- The user taps "Fechar" while the job is still "Pendente" or "Processando": the sheet dismisses and the in-flight job is left alone server-side; the app does not keep polling it in the background once the sheet is gone, and it is not treated as the "current" export if the sheet is reopened.
- The user taps the download icon again while an export sheet/job from a previous tap is still in flight for the same period: this does not create a second concurrent export job — the tap is treated as a no-op (or reopens the same in-flight sheet) rather than firing a second `POST /export/summary`.
- The session expires while the export sheet is open: the existing expired-session overlay (RF07) takes over exactly as it does for the rest of the screen; once re-authenticated, the sheet resumes reflecting the export job's real status rather than being stuck mid-attempt.
- The download itself (PDF or raw data) fails after the job reached a downloadable state (e.g., the signed URL expired or the connection drops mid-download): the corresponding button returns to a retryable state rather than leaving the sheet stuck or silently failing.
- Opening the export sheet, polling its job, or downloading a file does not alter My Records' list, its active filters, its sync badges, or its scroll position in any way.

states.md`, or the prototype extract leaves open.

## R1 — How the download endpoint's 302-redirect-to-signed-URL is fetched without leaking auth headers

**Decision**: `ApiClient` (core/network) gains one new method, `downloadFile(...)`, built the same way
`sseStream()` (RF04) added a second transport shape on top of the existing `call()` — a two-step fetch, never
a single `Dio.request<Map>()` (which expects JSON and would fail to parse PDF/raw bytes):
1. Request `GET /export/{jobId}/download?format=pdf|raw` with `followRedirects: false` and
   `validateStatus: (status) => status != null && status < 400` (so a 302 is accepted, not thrown as a
   `DioException`), sending the same `apikey`/`Authorization` headers every other call already sends — this
   leg talks to *our* backend function, so it goes through the exact same auth story as `call()`.
2. Read the `Location` response header. If the status was not 302 or the header is missing, treat it as a
   malformed response (`ValidationFailure`) — the backend's own contract only documents a 302 success shape.
3. Issue a **second**, header-less `Dio.request<List<int>>()` straight to that signed Storage URL, with
   `responseType: ResponseType.bytes` and no `apikey`/`Authorization` headers at all.
4. Return `Either<Failure, Uint8List>` — `Right(bytes)` on a 2xx from step 3; any failure from either leg maps
   through `_mapException` (step 1: identical to `call()`'s existing JSON-error path, so `AUTH_EXPIRED`/
   `NOT_FOUND`/etc. all resolve through the normal `ErrorMapper`) or a new, generic retryable
   `NetworkTimeoutFailure` (step 2/3: the storage leg never speaks this app's `{code, message, retryable}`
   error envelope, so there is nothing for `ErrorMapper` to parse — Edge Cases only asks that "the
   corresponding button returns to a retryable state", not that the exact backend error code survive a
   fetch that never reached the backend).

**Rationale**: the signed URL already encodes its own short-lived auth via query parameters (that is the
entire point of a signed URL); forwarding this app's `apikey`/`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`/user bearer token to a
third-party Storage host it was never intended for is an unnecessary credential-exposure surface Principle
III's spirit ("narrowly-accessed contract... prevents... credential leakage") argues against, and `dio`'s
default redirect-following would do exactly that by keeping the original request's headers across the
redirect. Disabling auto-redirect and manually re-issuing a clean request is the only way to control which
headers reach which host. This mirrors `sseStream()`'s own precedent of adding a second, download-agnostic
transport primitive to `ApiClient` rather than growing a parallel HTTP stack per feature.

**Alternatives considered**: letting `dio` auto-follow the redirect — rejected for the header-leak reason
above; a dedicated plain `http`/`http_client` package call for the storage leg — rejected, `dio` already does
a header-less byte-stream GET with no new dependency; parsing the Storage response as JSON first — rejected,
both `format=pdf` and `format=raw` are binary/text payloads to save to disk, not API responses with a
`{data: ...}` envelope.

## R2 — Saving/sharing the downloaded bytes (no download/file package exists yet)

**Decision**: add `share_plus: ^13.3.1` (new dependency; `path_provider` is already in `pubspec.yaml`, added
for the audio pipeline). A new data-layer class, `ExportFileRepositoryImpl` (behind a domain interface,
`ExportFileRepository`, so `ExportBloc` depends on it through the same mockable-repository shape every other
bloc already uses — never a bare plugin wrapper), writes the downloaded bytes to
`(await getTemporaryDirectory()).path` under a derived filename, then calls `Share.shareXFiles([XFile(path)])`
— the OS share sheet, satisfying the Assumption "trigger[s] the platform's standard way of saving or sharing a
downloaded file." The extension is taken from the response's own `content-type`/`content-disposition` header
when present, falling back to `.pdf` for `format=pdf` and `.json` for `format=raw` (every other endpoint in
this backend's contract speaks JSON; nothing in the OpenAPI spec names a different shape for the raw export).

**Rationale**: Constitution Principle II explicitly leaves "local cache... secure storage" (and, by the same
"choices not fixed here" logic, a file-share mechanism — no fixed package is named for this anywhere in
`docs/input/`) as an open implementation decision, the same category `image_picker`/`record`/`whisper_ggml`
were already added under in earlier units. `share_plus` is the de-facto standard Flutter package for exactly
this job (iOS `UIActivityViewController`), needs no new permission beyond what sharing already implies, and
composes with the already-present `path_provider` rather than introducing a second temp-file mechanism.

**Alternatives considered**: `open_file`/`open_filex` (opens a file in another app directly rather than
offering the OS share sheet) — rejected, narrower than "save or share" and typically requires a file-
association/viewer app to exist, which this PDF-generating unit cannot assume; writing to a permanent
app-documents path and leaving the user to find it in Files.app — rejected, no in-app file browser exists or
is in scope (Assumptions: "not responsible for building a custom in-app file viewer"), so a silent write with
no share/save prompt would be a dead end for the user.

## R3 — Status-polling mechanism and interval

**Decision**: `ExportBloc` polls `GET /export/{jobId}/status` through a self-rescheduling chain of internal
events, not `Timer.periodic` — the exact shape `RecordsBloc`'s own search debounce already establishes
(`Timer(duration, () => add(Event()))`, re-armed from inside the handler, cancelled in `close()`). The instant
`ExportRequested` is handled, the bloc emits `ExportPending()` synchronously (FR-004's "immediately after the
request"), awaits the `POST /export/summary` call, and on success immediately dispatches one
`ExportStatusPollTicked()` (no initial delay — the POST round-trip has already elapsed). Each tick's handler
calls `GET status` once; if the resulting job is not yet in a terminal state (`sheetState` below), it arms
`Timer(const Duration(seconds: 2), () => add(const ExportStatusPollTicked()))` for the next tick. Sequential,
never overlapping — a slow response is fully awaited before the next tick is even scheduled.

**Rationale**: spec.md's own Assumptions state this interval is "an implementation detail, not a product
requirement, as long as it is frequent enough that the user does not perceive the sheet as stuck" — 2 seconds
comfortably satisfies that for an AI-narrative job (seconds-to-tens-of-seconds scale) without hammering the
backend. Routing every tick through the bloc's own event pipeline (rather than a bare `Timer` mutating state
directly) keeps `ExportBloc` testable with `bloc_test` the same way `RecordsBloc`'s debounce already is —
`add()` from a `Timer` callback is this codebase's own established pattern, not a new one.

**Alternatives considered**: `Timer.periodic` — rejected, risks overlapping requests if a status call ever
takes longer than the interval (the sequential self-reschedule shape cannot overlap by construction); a
shorter interval (e.g. 500 ms) — rejected as needless backend load for a job whose fastest realistic path
(empty-period) never reaches polling at all (R6) and whose slowest path is bounded by an AI call, not network
latency.

## R4 — `ExportJob`'s pure sheet-state derivation, and the sixth, Clarification-resolved state

**Decision**: a pure domain extension, `ExportJob.sheetState`, mirrors the already-established
`DateRangeBounds.boundsAt`/`SyncBadge.derive` pattern (a total function over an enum, zero I/O, directly
unit-testable for RNF07) and implements `export-screen-states.md`'s table verbatim:

| `status` | `narrativeStatus` | `sheetState` |
|---|---|---|
| `pending` | (any) | `pendente` |
| `processing` | (any) | `processando` |
| `dataReady` | `processing` | `processando` (Assumption: no early download link; still visually "Processando") |
| `done` | `done` | `concluido` |
| `done` | `failed` or `skipped` | `erroNarrativa` (FR-006 — the prototype's single "Erro" state) |
| `error` | — | `erroCompleto` (FR-007 — the Clarification-resolved sixth state) |

`erroCompleto` is a distinct enum value from `erroNarrativa` even though the prototype's own catalog names
only one "Erro" state — this directly encodes spec.md's resolved Clarification ("reusing the error color/icon
family, with copy distinct from FR-006's... no PDF/raw buttons, and only... Fechar"). `ExportBloc` additionally
reaches `erroCompleto` from two paths `ExportJob.sheetState` never sees at all, because no job/jobId exists
yet at that point: an `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD`-shaped `POST` failure instead maps to a seventh, job-independent
bloc state, `periodoVazio` (R6), and any *other* `POST /export/summary` failure (timeout, offline, rate-
limited, ...) maps directly to the bloc's `erroCompleto` state without ever creating a job (R6).

**Rationale**: putting the five-row mapping in the domain layer as a pure getter (not duplicated inline in
`ExportBloc` or a widget's `switch`) is the same choice `RecordsBloc` already made for `SyncBadge.derive` and
`DateRangeBounds` — directly testable, and the one place this mapping's correctness is asserted. Keeping
`erroCompleto`/`periodoVazio` as *bloc*-level states rather than trying to force them into `ExportJob` is
necessary because both can occur with no `ExportJob` ever existing (a job is never created for an empty
period, and a POST that never got as far as `202 Accepted` never produced a `jobId` to poll).

**Alternatives considered**: reusing one single `erro` state for both FR-006 and FR-007 with a boolean flag —
rejected, directly contradicts the resolved Clarification's explicit "this state MUST be visually and
functionally distinct from FR-006's narrative-only failure" (FR-007); modeling `periodoVazio` as a sentinel
`ExportJob` (e.g. a fake job with no id) — rejected, forces every `ExportJob` consumer to special-case a
value that was never a real job, when the bloc's own sealed `ExportState` already has a natural home for it.

## R5 — Routing every `POST /export/summary` failure other than `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` to FR-007

**Decision**: if the initial `POST /export/summary` call itself fails with `ExportEmptyPeriodFailure`, the
bloc emits `ExportEmptyPeriod()` (FR-003) and polls nothing. If it fails with `AuthExpiredFailure` after the
repository's one silent-refresh retry already failed, the bloc fires `reauthRequired` (R7) same as every other
failure path in this app, *and* also emits `ExportFailed()` — the session overlay takes over visually (FR-012)
regardless of what state sits underneath it. For every other failure shape (`NetworkTimeoutFailure`,
`NetworkOfflineFailure`, `RateLimitedFailure`, `ValidationFailure`, ...), the bloc emits `ExportFailed()`
(FR-007's generic, job-independent failure state) directly — no job/jobId exists, so "no data was produced" is
true by construction, matching FR-007's own wording precisely.

**Rationale**: spec.md's FRs/Assumptions describe FR-007 only in terms of a job that "fails entirely," which
textually presumes a job exists — but the spec is silent on what happens if the export is never even accepted
in the first place (e.g. the device goes offline the instant the download icon is tapped). Reasonable
technical judgment under Principle I: a request that never produced a job has, definitionally, produced no
data and no narrative — the exact condition FR-007 itself describes — so reusing that same terminal state
(rather than inventing an eighth, undocumented sheet state) is the simplest construction that satisfies FR-010
("Fechar... present... in every one of the five sheet states") without adding a state the prototype's own
five-state catalog, plus the one Clarification-resolved addition, doesn't already cover.

**Alternatives considered**: a distinct "could not even start" state — rejected, no product input describes
one, and FR-007's own generic, errorCode-agnostic copy ("shown the same way regardless of the backend's
specific error code") already reads naturally for this case too; silently retrying the POST — rejected, not
asked for anywhere, and would hide a real failure (e.g. persistent offline) behind an indefinite "Pendente",
directly risking SC-005's "never... indefinitely" guarantee.

## R6 — Why `ExportBloc` is sheet-scoped (one new instance per `showModalBottomSheet` call), not a singleton

**Decision**: `ExportBloc` is `get_it`-registered with `registerFactory` (a fresh instance per
`getIt<ExportBloc>()` call) — the same registration shape `InsertionModalBloc`/`VaultBloc` already use for
their own modal/one-shot screens — and is provided directly above the bottom sheet's content
(`BlocProvider<ExportBloc>(create: (_) => getIt<ExportBloc>()..add(ExportRequested(...)))`, mirroring
`FilterSheet`'s own self-contained-sheet shape). Its polling `Timer` is cancelled in `close()` (same pattern
`RecordsBloc` already uses for its debounce timer); `close()` fires the moment the sheet's `BlocProvider` is
removed from the tree (i.e. the sheet is dismissed), so no poll ever fires for a sheet the user has already
closed — directly satisfying the Edge Case "the app does not keep polling it in background once the sheet is
gone... not treated as the 'current' export if the sheet is reopened." FR-011's "repeated taps... MUST NOT
create multiple concurrent export jobs" is satisfied one layer up, in `_RecordsPageState`: a simple
`bool _isOpeningExportSheet` guard (set before `await showModalBottomSheet(...)`, cleared after) around the
download icon's `onPressed`, identical in spirit to the guard every `IconButton`-triggered async action in
this codebase already needs against a double-tap racing a single `await`.

**Rationale**: the Edge Case's own wording offers two acceptable shapes ("treated as a no-op (or reopens the
same in-flight sheet)"); the no-op-via-guarded-tap shape is simpler and needs no new cross-sheet state
(reusing a leftover job id across sheet instances would directly contradict the Assumptions' own "Reopening the
export sheet afterward is a fresh request; it does not need to return to a leftover job" — the two Edge
Cases/Assumptions together only make sense together if "in flight" here means "the sheet currently on screen,"
not "any job the backend still happens to be processing"). A page-level singleton bloc (reused across sheet
opens, like `EntriesRepositoryImpl`'s `cachedEntries`) was considered and rejected because the ephemeral,
one-shot-per-open shape of the export sheet (Key Entities: "ephemeral... never shown anywhere outside the
export sheet") has no state worth surviving a dismiss — unlike `EntriesRepositoryImpl`'s cache, which exists
specifically to survive across many screen visits.

**Alternatives considered**: a `RecordsBloc`-owned export sub-state (folding export into the existing bloc
entirely) — rejected, conflates two independently-failing, independently-lifetimed concerns into one state
class, the same reasoning RF04's research.md R7 already used to keep `ChatBloc`/`ChatSessionsBloc` apart; a
page-level singleton `ExportBloc` surviving sheet dismissal — rejected per the Assumptions conflict above.

## R7 — Reusing the exact `reauthRequired`/silent-refresh-retry shape, start to finish

**Decision**: `ExportRepositoryImpl` wraps every one of its three calls (`create`/`status`/`download`) in the
identical `_retryAfterSilentRefresh` shape `EntriesRepositoryImpl` already established (exactly one retry via
`SessionRepository.refresh()` on a first-attempt `AuthExpiredFailure`; a second `AuthExpiredFailure` after that
retry is returned as-is, no loop). `ExportBloc` owns its own one-shot `_reauthController`/`reauthRequired`
stream (`StreamController<void>.broadcast()`, closed in `close()`), fired with `if (failure is
AuthExpiredFailure) _reauthController.add(null);` at every call site that can produce one — the exact line
`RecordsBloc` already uses three times over. The sheet widget (`ExportSheet`, a `StatefulWidget`) subscribes
to it in `initState()` exactly as `RecordsPage` already does for `RecordsBloc`, dispatching
`SessionBloc.add(const AuthExpiredDetected())` — `SessionBloc` is provided above `MaterialApp.router` in
`main.dart`, so it is reachable from a bottom sheet's `BuildContext` exactly as it is from any full-screen
route, and the resulting "Sessão expirada" overlay (pushed via the root `NavigatorKey`) renders above the
sheet automatically, needing no export-specific wiring.

**Rationale**: FR-012 asks for exactly this — the existing RF07 mechanism "tak[ing] over exactly as it does
elsewhere on the screen" — so the correct implementation is to reuse the identical mechanism verbatim, not to
build a parallel one. "Resume reflecting the export job's actual status once re-authenticated" falls out of
this construction for free: `ExportRepositoryImpl`'s own retry-after-refresh means a mid-poll `AUTH_EXPIRED`
that the silent refresh *can* recover from is invisible to `ExportBloc` entirely (the very next poll tick
simply succeeds with fresh credentials); only a refresh that itself fails surfaces the overlay, and once the
user re-authenticates through it, the next scheduled poll tick (already armed before the failure, since the
`Timer` from the prior successful tick is independent of this one failing) picks the real status back up with
no bespoke "resume" code needed.

**Alternatives considered**: having `ExportBloc` itself call `SessionRepository.refresh()` — rejected, 
duplicates logic `EntriesRepositoryImpl`/`ChatRepositoryImpl` already centralize at the repository layer,
and would be the first bloc in this codebase to depend on `SessionRepository` directly, contradicting the
established "blocs never touch `SessionRepository`" shape (research.md precedent, `RecordsBloc`'s own
docstring).

## R8 — How the download icon learns the current period, and why no new `go_router` route is added

**Decision**: the export sheet is opened from `RecordsPage`'s existing header `IconButton` (currently an inert
placeholder, `records_page.dart`'s `_Header`), not via a new route. `_RecordsPageState` reads
`context.read<RecordsBloc>().state`'s `dateRange` (a `DateRangeOption`, already RF06's own filter model) at
the moment the icon is tapped, converts it with the already-existing, pure `DateRangeBounds.boundsAt(DateTime.
now())` extension (RF06) into `(from: DateTime?, to: DateTime?)`, and passes those two nullable values straight
through to `ExportSheet(periodStart: ..., periodEnd: ...)` as `showModalBottomSheet`'s builder argument — the
sheet's own `ExportBloc` dispatches `ExportRequested(periodStart, periodEnd)` from its `initState`.

**Rationale**: spec.md's own Assumptions state the export "exports whatever period My Records' own active
date filter currently represents... rather than offering a separate period picker inside the sheet itself" —
`RecordsBloc`'s `dateRange` is already the single source of truth for that filter (FR-002's own wording,
RF06), and `DateRangeBounds` already converts it to concrete bounds for every other consumer that needs them.
Reusing it here needs zero new domain logic. A bottom sheet (not a route) matches both the prototype
("bottom sheet over Tela 4") and this codebase's own precedent for `FilterSheet` — no `go_router` route exists
for RF06's filter sheet either, for the same reason.

**Alternatives considered**: giving `ExportSheet` its own `SessionRepository`-free copy of date-bounds logic
— rejected, duplicates `DateRangeBounds` for no benefit; a new parameterized route (e.g. `/records/export`) —
rejected, same reasoning RF04's research.md R7 already used against a `/home/:sessionId` route: it would force
`go_router` to own state (the active period) a bottom sheet's constructor argument already carries perfectly
well, for a screen that is visually and functionally a modal, not a navigable destination.

# Data Model: P-RF05 — Personal summary export

Source: spec.md §Key Entities/§Requirements; requirements.md §§1 (RF05), 6.5, 8, 13;
`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`'s `/export/*` schemas; `docs/input/backend/export-screen-states.md`;
`docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`; `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §2.5; `research.md`. This
unit adds one new feature folder, `lib/features/export/`, and two small, reused-as-is extensions to existing
`core/` and `records/` code (R1, R8) — it introduces no change to any existing domain entity.

## `ExportJobStatus` / `NarrativeStatus` / `ExportJob` (`lib/features/export/domain/entities/export_job.dart`) — NEW

```dart
enum ExportJobStatus { pending, processing, dataReady, done, error }
enum NarrativeStatus { pending, processing, done, failed, skipped }
enum ExportSheetState { pendente, processando, concluido, erroNarrativa, erroCompleto, periodoVazio }

class ExportJob extends Equatable {
  const ExportJob({
    required this.jobId,
    required this.status,
    required this.narrativeStatus,
    required this.entryCount,
    required this.errorCode,
    required this.narrativeErrorCode,
    required this.downloadAvailable,
  });

  final String jobId;
  final ExportJobStatus status;
  final NarrativeStatus narrativeStatus;
  final int? entryCount;
  final String? errorCode;
  final String? narrativeErrorCode;
  final bool downloadAvailable;

  @override
  List<Object?> get props =>
      [jobId, status, narrativeStatus, entryCount, errorCode, narrativeErrorCode, downloadAvailable];
}

extension ExportJobSheetState on ExportJob {
  /// Pure, total mapping of `export-screen-states.md`'s own table (research.md R4) — the one place this
  /// mapping's correctness is asserted (RNF07). `periodoVazio` and the job-independent branch of
  /// `erroCompleto` are never produced here — see `ExportState` below.
  ExportSheetState get sheetState => switch ((status, narrativeStatus)) {
    (ExportJobStatus.pending, _) => ExportSheetState.pendente,
    (ExportJobStatus.processing, _) => ExportSheetState.processando,
    (ExportJobStatus.dataReady, _) => ExportSheetState.processando,
    (ExportJobStatus.done, NarrativeStatus.done) => ExportSheetState.concluido,
    (ExportJobStatus.done, _) => ExportSheetState.erroNarrativa,
    (ExportJobStatus.error, _) => ExportSheetState.erroCompleto,
  };
}
```

- `status`/`narrativeStatus` parse 1:1 from `GET /export/{jobId}/status`'s own enum values (`pending`/
  `processing`/`data_ready`/`done`/`error`; `pending`/`processing`/`done`/`failed`/`skipped`) — `dataReady` is
  the Dart-cased form of the wire value `data_ready`.
- `downloadAvailable`/`entryCount`/`errorCode`/`narrativeErrorCode` are carried straight through for
  completeness (e.g. future logging) but `sheetState` alone drives every rendering decision this unit needs —
  FR-007 is explicit that `errorCode` is never shown or branched on ("shown the same way regardless of the
  backend's specific error code").

## `ExportRepository` (`lib/features/export/domain/repositories/export_repository.dart`) — NEW

```dart
abstract class ExportRepository {
  Future<Either<Failure, String>> create({
    required DateTime? periodStart,
    required DateTime? periodEnd,
  }); // returns the new jobId

  Future<Either<Failure, ExportJob>> status(String jobId);

  Future<Either<Failure, Uint8List>> download({required String jobId, required ExportFormat format});
}

enum ExportFormat { pdf, raw }
```

- **`create`** → `POST /export/summary` (`export-summary-create`), body `{periodStart, periodEnd,
  includeNarrative: true}` — `periodStart`/`periodEnd` are sent as explicit JSON `null` (not omitted) when the
  period is "all time," since both are in the OpenAPI schema's `required` list despite being `nullable: true`
  (contracts/export-repository.md's exact request shape). `includeNarrative: true` is sent explicitly even
  though it is already the schema's own default, so this unit's one request shape self-documents FR-002's
  "including the narrative by default" rather than relying silently on a default it never asserts.
  `EXPORT_EMPTY_PERIOD` (400) surfaces as `ExportEmptyPeriodFailure` — already defined in `core/network/
  failure.dart` (added as part of this app's shared, closed 13-code taxonomy before this unit existed).
- **`status`** → `GET /export/{jobId}/status` (`export-status-get`), `pathSegments: [jobId]`.
- **`download`** → `ApiClient.downloadFile` (R1), `pathSegments: [jobId]`, `queryParameters: {'format':
  format.name}`.
- All three retry exactly once through `SessionRepository.refresh()` on `AuthExpiredFailure` before giving up
  (research.md R7) — see `contracts/export-repository.md` for the exact sequence, identical in shape to
  `EntriesRepositoryImpl`'s.

### `ExportRemoteDataSource` (`lib/features/export/data/export_remote_data_source.dart`) — NEW

Calls `ApiClient.call`/`ApiClient.downloadFile` and parses `ExportJob` from the status response's `data`
object; `create` parses `data.jobId`; `download` passes bytes through unparsed.

### `ExportRepositoryImpl` (`lib/features/export/data/export_repository_impl.dart`) — NEW

Depends on `ExportRemoteDataSource` + `SessionRepository` (the cross-feature domain interface, same shape
`EntriesRepositoryImpl` already depends on it) — no local cache (Key Entities: "ephemeral... never shown
anywhere outside the export sheet"; unlike `EntriesRepositoryImpl`/`ChatRepositoryImpl`, there is nothing here
worth persisting across a process restart).

## `ExportFileRepository` (`lib/features/export/domain/repositories/export_file_repository.dart`) — NEW

```dart
abstract class ExportFileRepository {
  Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> share({required Uint8List bytes, required ExportFormat format});
}
```

### `ExportFileRepositoryImpl` (`lib/features/export/data/export_file_repository_impl.dart`) — NEW

Writes `bytes` to a temp file (`path_provider`'s `getTemporaryDirectory()`), named
`cerne-resumo.<ext>`/`cerne-dados.<ext>` (`.pdf` for `ExportFormat.pdf`; `.json` for `ExportFormat.raw`,
research.md R2), then calls `Share.shareXFiles([XFile(path)])` (`share_plus`). Any `PlatformException`/I/O
failure (disk full, share sheet dismissed with an error — not a plain user cancel, which `share_plus` reports
as a normal, non-throwing result) maps to a retryable failure the same way R1's storage leg does — never a
new, undocumented `Failure` subtype.

## `ApiClient` — extended (`lib/core/network/api_client.dart`)

```dart
Future<Either<Failure, Uint8List>> downloadFile(
  String function, {
  List<String>? pathSegments,
  Map<String, dynamic>? queryParameters,
  AuthMode authMode = AuthMode.userSession,
})
```

`call()`/`sseStream()` are unchanged. See `contracts/http-client-download-extension.md` for the exact
two-step, no-header-leak sequence (research.md R1).

## `ExportEvent` (`lib/features/export/presentation/bloc/export_event.dart`) — NEW

| Event | When |
|---|---|
| `ExportRequested(periodStart, periodEnd)` | `ExportSheet.initState` — the one and only time a job is requested for that sheet instance. |

2	# Research: P-RF05 — Personal summary export
3	
4	Phase 0 output. Each item is a reasonable technical decision made under Constitution Principle I ("where
5	these documents are silent, implementers MUST make a reasonable technical decision rather than block on
6	clarification"). None reopens spec.md's own already-resolved Clarification (the FR-007 full-failure state) —

9	
10	## R1 — How the download endpoint's 302-redirect-to-signed-URL is fetched without leaking auth headers
11	
12	**Decision**: `ApiClient` (core/network) gains one new method, `downloadFile(...)`, built the same way
13	`sseStream()` (RF04) added a second transport shape on top of the existing `call()` — a two-step fetch, never
14	a single `Dio.request<Map>()` (which expects JSON and would fail to parse PDF/raw bytes):
15	1. Request `GET /export/{jobId}/download?format=pdf|raw` with `followRedirects: false` and
16	   `validateStatus: (status) => status != null && status < 400` (so a 302 is accepted, not thrown as a
17	   `DioException`), sending the same `apikey`/`Authorization` headers every other call already sends — this
18	   leg talks to *our* backend function, so it goes through the exact same auth story as `call()`.
19	2. Read the `Location` response header. If the status was not 302 or the header is missing, treat it as a
20	   malformed response (`ValidationFailure`) — the backend's own contract only documents a 302 success shape.
21	3. Issue a **second**, header-less `Dio.request<List<int>>()` straight to that signed Storage URL, with
22	   `responseType: ResponseType.bytes` and no `apikey`/`Authorization` headers at all.
23	4. Return `Either<Failure, Uint8List>` — `Right(bytes)` on a 2xx from step 3; any failure from either leg maps
24	   through `_mapException` (step 1: identical to `call()`'s existing JSON-error path, so `AUTH_EXPIRED`/
25	   `NOT_FOUND`/etc. all resolve through the normal `ErrorMapper`) or a new, generic retryable
26	   `NetworkTimeoutFailure` (step 2/3: the storage leg never speaks this app's `{code, message, retryable}`
27	   error envelope, so there is nothing for `ErrorMapper` to parse — Edge Cases only asks that "the
28	   corresponding button returns to a retryable state", not that the exact backend error code survive a
29	   fetch that never reached the backend).
30	
31	**Rationale**: the signed URL already encodes its own short-lived auth via query parameters (that is the
32	entire point of a signed URL); forwarding this app's `apikey`/`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`/user bearer token to a
33	third-party Storage host it was never intended for is an unnecessary credential-exposure surface Principle
34	III's spirit ("narrowly-accessed contract... prevents... credential leakage") argues against, and `dio`'s
35	default redirect-following would do exactly that by keeping the original request's headers across the
36	redirect. Disabling auto-redirect and manually re-issuing a clean request is the only way to control which
37	headers reach which host. This mirrors `sseStream()`'s own precedent of adding a second, download-agnostic
38	transport primitive to `ApiClient` rather than growing a parallel HTTP stack per feature.
39	
40	**Alternatives considered**: letting `dio` auto-follow the redirect — rejected for the header-leak reason
41	above; a dedicated plain `http`/`http_client` package call for the storage leg — rejected, `dio` already does
42	a header-less byte-stream GET with no new dependency; parsing the Storage response as JSON first — rejected,
43	both `format=pdf` and `format=raw` are binary/text payloads to save to disk, not API responses with a
44	`{data: ...}` envelope.
45	
46	## R2 — Saving/sharing the downloaded bytes (no download/file package exists yet)
47	
48	**Decision**: add `share_plus: ^13.3.1` (new dependency; `path_provider` is already in `pubspec.yaml`, added
